question: Can the noncompact round-sphere BT bubble be periodized by replacing squared radius with the standard chordal torus distance, and what local jet condition is required to remove any new Euler-gradient divergence?
answer: The standard chord periodization fails: its quartic harmonic defect forces ||E_m||_2^2=(128*pi^2/5)*log(1/m)+O(1), while ||R_m||_2^2 stays bounded and retains the round-bubble concentration. The unique two-harmonic fourth-order stencil cancels the quartic defect and makes the local Euler-gradient contribution uniformly square-integrable. This repairs the local bubble but does not decide the complete global torus quotient or the Witten/Gibbs estimate.
